Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CP-Guard+: A New Paradigm for Malicious Agent Detection and Defense in Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Collaborative perception (CP) is a promising approach for safe connected and autonomous driving that enables multiple connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) to share sensing information with each other to enhance perception performance. For example, occluded objects can be detected, and the sensing range can be extended. However, compared with single-agent perception, the openness of a CP system makes it more vulnerable to malicious agents and attackers, who can inject malicious information to mislead the perception of an ego CAV, resulting in severe risks for the safety of autonomous driving systems. To mitigate the vulnerability of CP systems, we first propose a new paradigm for malicious agent detection that effectively identifies malicious agents at the feature level without requiring verification of final perception results, significantly reducing computational overhead. Building on this paradigm, we introduce CP-GuardBench, the first comprehensive dataset for training and evaluating various malicious agent detection methods for CP systems. Furthermore, we develop a robust defense method called CP-Guard+, which enhances the margin between the representations of benign and malicious features through a carefully designed dual-centered contrastive loss. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on both CP-GuardBench and V2X-Sim, and the results demonstrate the superiority of CP-Guard+.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted for IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of a station's cell wets its soil as natural storms wet the probes. Replace either piece and the forecasts stay, but the meaning goes: with neural operators, only a probe fitted to the stations finds the soil water; with a generic recurrent transition, rain on a single cell barely moves it. Yet when the same rain covers the whole region the two transitions swap roles, and the conserving one responds too weakly. Grounding makes a world model readable; its response to actions must be tested under more than one kind of intervention.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LCM-UNet: Scale-Selective Mamba with Reparameterizable Multi-Basis Local Modeling for Lightweight Skin Lesion Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Accurate lesion segmentation underpins automated dermoscopic analysis: masks enable measurements of asymmetry, border and size. Deployment in primary care or on mobile devices requires a compact network. Existing ultra-light Mamba U-Nets offer global context, but global-modeling cost depends on each Mamba block's resolution, while their local branches rely on a single square kernel. We introduce LCM-UNet, a 33,474-parameter U-shaped network that fuses every skip at its native resolution, restricts bidirectional Mamba to stages at one-sixteenth of the input resolution or coarser, and uses local convolutions at finer scales. A multi-basis reparameterizable adapter augments each local branch during training with dilated, horizontal and vertical depthwise kernels, then folds them into the host kernel before inference. Each skip connection also learns a stage-specific gain. Nine networks were retrained on the official ISIC 2017 and ISIC 2018 partitions under a harmonized protocol, with PH$^2$ reserved for external validation and ablations run on a development split. LCM-UNet achieved Dice scores of 88.62%, 89.73% and 90.46% on ISIC 2017, ISIC 2018 and PH$^2$, respectively, ranking first on both ISIC test sets and second on PH$^2$ among the compared models. In the native-resolution host, removing Mamba from the one-eighth-resolution decoder stage eliminated 63% of Mamba operations, corresponding to 5.3% of all operations, with a Dice change of $-0.03$ percentage points. The adapter improved Dice by 0.48 percentage points over a single host kernel without adding deployed parameters or operations. With latency so far measured only on a GPU, LCM-UNet is a candidate for resource-constrained deployment.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: The authors request the withdrawal of this manuscript due to unresolved methodological and experimental validation concerns that may affect the reliability of the reported findings. The authors consider it inappropriate to retain the current version as an active preprint until these concerns have been adequately addressed

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BGD-SF PolySegNet: boundary-guided dynamic selective fusion network for robust polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Effective polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images is crucial for early detection of colorectal cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. While current deep learning models perform well on traditional Dice benchmarks, border segmentation remains difficult. Most methods use boundary information only as an additional loss signal during training, which prevents the network from explicitly learning border-guided feature selection or mask refinement. This paper introduces BGD-SF PolySegNet, a boundary-guided encoder-decoder architecture that controls three phases of the segmentation pipeline: dynamic multi-scale context aggregation, selective skip-feature fusion, and final mask refinement. The architecture comprises a pretrained EfficientNet-B4 backbone and three proposed modules: Boundary-Guided Dynamic Cascaded Multi-Scale Context Aggregation (BGD-CMSCA), Boundary-Guided Selective Attention Fusion (BG-SAGF), and a Multi-Level Boundary Guidance Head (MBGH). The model is trained on 3,535 annotated images from Kvasir-SEG, BKAI-IGH NeoPolyp-Small, and PolypGen, and evaluated on four held-out benchmark datasets. On the internal test set, BGD-SF achieves a Dice of 0.887, IoU of 0.839, mask-derived Boundary F1 of 0.531, HD95 of 30.32, and ASSD of 18.10, improving Boundary F1, HD95, and ASSD by 15.7%, 27.5%, and 34.6% over the strongest CNN baselines. External validation on CVC-ClinicDB, CVC-ColonDB, ETIS-Larib, and CVC-300 yielded Dice scores of 0.891, 0.776, 0.863, and 0.885, respectively. The model runs at 35 FPS with 22.51M parameters. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirm statistically significant mask-derived Boundary F1 improvements over six of seven ablation variants (p < 0.001; small-to-moderate effect sizes, r = 0.215-0.434), demonstrating that integrating boundary guidance as an active architectural component measurably advances polyp boundary delineation.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: The authors request the withdrawal of this manuscript due to unresolved methodological and experimental validation concerns that may affect the reliability of the reported findings. The authors consider it inappropriate to retain the current version as an active preprint until these concerns have been adequately addressed

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Practice in Text, Act in Pixels: Correcting Where Perception Fails
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: GUI agents can learn cheaply from a text view of an interface and act on screenshots through a vision-language screen reader. Yet on a simulated mobile platform with a low-cost reader, policies that complete most tasks in text fail on many of the same tasks on screenshots. We ask where a small budget of real screenshots is best spent to close this gap. We find that the reader's misreads are systematic and recur on the same interface elements. Noise matched to the reader's error rates, a natural sim-to-real remedy, misses this structure, and in a pre-specified comparison it did not beat training the policy directly on screenshots. We therefore correct the misreads at their source with reader alignment, which fine-tunes the reader on screenshots paired with their text views. The reader learns to output each screen's text view, as in text practice, and the policy stays unchanged. Spent on the reader, the screenshot budget gives 80.9% full-task success on new task instances, against 55.6% when spent on training the policy. Given the same labeled screenshots, adapting the reader also beats adapting the policy, and a single aligned reader improves every text-trained policy we tried without retraining any of them.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 26 pages, 9 figures, 21 tables. Code: https://github.com/Carlxuzhl/practice-in-text ; aligned reader: https://huggingface.co/xuzhl/practice-in-text-aligned-reader ; v2: adds Appendix L (further tests of reader alignment)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Region-aware error triage for medical image segmentation with groupwise conformal risk control
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Segmentation masks are increasingly reviewed rather than redrawn, which requires knowing where a mask is likely wrong. Learned error maps rank pixels by risk, but the number of pixels to warn is chosen ad hoc, and calibrating one warning threshold over all error pixels may leave errors far from the predicted contour under-flagged. We propose RACE-Triage, a post-hoc error triage framework that leaves the segmentation mask unchanged. A risk network is trained on out-of-fold predictions from backbone-independent inputs. The predicted contour partitions each image into a boundary band and a non-boundary region, and conformal risk control is applied separately in each region to bound the expected fraction of missed errors among cases with errors there. On ISIC 2018 dermoscopy and BUSI breast ultrasound (where patient identifiers are unavailable, so independence across images is assumed), pooled control met its overall target but missed on average 31.8% and 36.4% of non-boundary errors. Regional control reduced these fractions to 19.3% and 20.9% and raised the recall of size-filtered false-negative components from 0.722 to 0.818 and from 0.611 to 0.763. The mean warned area grew by 1.6 and 4.9 percentage points, and its 95th percentile reached 23.5% and 38.5%. The effect held across three seeds and a second backbone, and area-matched heuristics did not reproduce it. On the external PH$^2$ set, frozen thresholds exceeded both targets, whereas recalibration with 100 local images brought the mean over repeated splits below them. Regional calibration improves non-boundary error coverage at a measured increase in warned area.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: The authors request the withdrawal of this manuscript due to unresolved methodological and experimental validation concerns that may affect the reliability of the reported findings. The authors consider it inappropriate to retain the current version as an active preprint until these concerns have been adequately addressed

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Conditional Evidence Reconstruction and Decomposition for Interpretable Multimodal Diagnosis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Neurobiological and neurodegenerative diseases are inherently multifactorial, arising from coupled influences spanning genetic susceptibility, brain alterations, and environmental and behavioral factors. Multimodal modeling has therefore been increasingly adopted for disease diagnosis by integrating complementary evidence across data sources. However, in both large-scale cohorts and real-world clinical workflows, modality coverage is often incomplete, making many multimodal models brittle when one or more modalities are unavailable. Existing approaches to incomplete multimodal diagnosis typically rely on group-wise or static priors, which may fail to capture subject-specific cross-modal dependencies; moreover, many models provide limited interpretability into which evidence sources drive the final decision. To address these limitations, we propose Conditional Evidence Reconstruction and Decomposition (CERD), a framework for interpretable multimodal diagnosis with incomplete modalities. CERD first reconstructs missing modality representations conditioned on each subject's observed inputs, then decomposes diagnostic evidence into shared cross-modal corroboration and modality-specific cues via logit-level attribution. Experiments on the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) demonstrate that CERD outperforms competitive baselines under incomplete-modality settings while producing structured and clinically aligned evidence attributions for trustworthy decision support.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the agent's model, prompt, or action space. NightWatch couples the VLM agent with NightWatch-0.8B, a lightweight System-1 model that performs streaming monitoring of the interface state and keeps the agent synchronized with the evolving environment at low computational cost and latency, thereby grounding each decision in the current state rather than an outdated snapshot and reducing both stale actions and idle waiting while preserving task success. Experiments on desktop and dynamic web environments (OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench) show that NightWatch, driven by a watcher of only 0.8B parameters, reduces non-reasoning wall-clock time by 33% and wasted time by 53% on OSWorld while keeping task success on par, raises success on DynaCU-Bench from 39.5% to 44.2% with the large VLM agent, and is more efficient than passive-watching baselines such as AOI and PUSV under the same screenshot-only input, as well as a System-1 decision model more than $30\times$ its size. Overall, NightWatch demonstrates that the timing of perception is as critical as its content, marking a step toward agents that maintain continuous awareness of their environment rather than perceiving it turn by turn.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SANA-Robot: Efficient World Action Model with Hybrid Memory
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World action models (WAMs) leverage the world knowledge of video generation models to improve action generation by aligning visual prediction with action prediction. However, their prediction overhead prevents real-time deployment on edge devices, and they usually lack an effective long-term memory. We introduce SANA-Robot, a 4.5B WAM with minute-level memory that runs in real time on edge devices, built on the following core designs: (1) hybrid memory at constant cost: our WAM relies on linear attention to maintain a global memory with a fixed-size state, and on sliding window softmax attention layers that propagate previous information, enabling high success rates on tasks requiring whole-episode memory while keeping an efficient and constant inference speed; (2) a unified model: by dynamically applying different noise levels to action and video tokens, SANA-Robot can serve not only as a policy but also as a world simulator; (3) a full-stack infrastructure for both memory training and inference, including efficient data packing and shuffling as well as memory-phase-based asynchronous execution. SANA-Robot achieves the best performance on the memory dimension of RoboDojo among models of medium size (about 5B) and the highest success rates on LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro and LIBERO-Max. In real-world deployment, SANA-Robot takes 135 ms per action chunk on an RTX 5090 with FP8 GEMMs and 115 ms with NVFP4 GEMMs, and achieves closed-loop, real-time asynchronous robot control at 30 Hz on edge devices, demonstrating both the efficiency and the effectiveness of SANA-Robot. Project page: https://nvlabs.github.io/Sana/Robot/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: XShot: Cross-Shot Video Object Insertion from a Reference Video
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present XShot, a framework for cross-shot video object insertion, which adds objects to a shot by watching another shot of the same scene. Video productions show a scene through many shots, and objects added to one shot must appear consistently in the others. Most video editors take the appearance of new objects from reference images and their location from a text prompt, a mask or an edited keyframe, leaving this consistency to the user. XShot reads both from a reference video of another shot, which need not be aligned with the target, and needs no mask, box or camera pose. We build on a video Diffusion Transformer and formulate the task as in-context generation over the reference video, a few images of the objects and the target video. A geometry-aware cross-shot attention estimates the epipolar geometry between the two shots from the model's own correspondences and uses it to guide where the target reads the reference and the exemplars. We train XShot with an erase-and-restore data engine: objects are erased from one shot of a film or a multi-camera recording and restored from another shot of the scene. Experiments show that XShot places objects more accurately and renders them more faithfully than open-source and commercial video editors, while leaving the rest of the shot intact.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Let Androids Dream: From Visual Elements to Emergent Implications via Contextual Alignment
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image metaphor understanding differs from general VQA: the implied meaning is rarely explicit in pixels and instead emerges from the compositional interaction of visual elements together with social intent and culture-specific background. We identify missing context, namely conventions already in a model's weights that single-pass inference leaves unused and external facts absent from the weights, as a failure mode of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We formalize Contextual Alignment as inference over a latent context: selecting background knowledge relevant to the image's composition and useful for inferring its implication. We then propose Let Androids Dream (LAD), a training-free framework that operationalizes contextual alignment through test-time computation: (1) Perception extracts compositional visual structure, (2) Search adaptively acquires context from parametric knowledge or web search, and (3) Reasoning aligns compositions with context to derive emergent implications. On the bilingual S100 benchmark, LAD raises the lightweight GPT-4o-mini from 44% to 74% (English) and from 42% to 52% (Chinese) Multiple-Choice Question (MCQ) accuracy, on par with the closed-book GPT-5.4 in English, and from 2.98 to 4.02 and from 3.36 to 3.66 on Open-Style Questions (OSQ). LAD improves all five backbones we test, including the open-source Qwen2.5-VL-7B (+18 MCQ and +1.30 OSQ points in English) and Gemini-3.0-Pro, where it obtains the highest OSQ scores (4.30 and 4.46), and its gains hold on the full II-Bench and CII-Bench. Adding other search tools raises MCQ accuracy in five of six cases but changes OSQ scores by -0.48 to +0.01, whereas LAD's search stage improves both, suggesting that how context is acquired matters beyond access to search. LAD with web search also improves MMMU, SeedBench, and MMStar. We open-sourced all code and datasets at https://ming-zch.github.io/lad.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PIAE: Physics-Informed Continuous Autoencoding for Compact 3D Human Motion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Temporal compression reduces the sequence length that motion generators must model, but can damage articulated detail and global trajectory. These errors have unequal consequences: root-velocity and heading errors propagate through trajectory recovery and affect the placement of the entire body. We propose PIAE, a physics-informed continuous autoencoder that allocates a fixed token budget between explicitly retained kinematic signals and complementary learned features. At 8 x temporal compression, each 256-dimensional token contains 224 learned values and a 32-dimensional physical carrier. The complete token conditions neural decoding, while a parallel recovery path constrains selected outputs. On the official HumanML3D benchmark, PIAE achieves 8.936 mm global MPJPE, an 82.0% reduction relative to a same-width learned-only model. The benefit extends beyond trajectory restoration: facing-local neural-body error before analytical correction decreases by 76.6% in a frozen-checkpoint validation diagnostic, and supplying the same true trajectory to both models preserves the body-quality advantage. Targeted root-only and explicit-root hybrid controls establish strong trajectory-aware comparisons; alternative carriers reveal that torso references favor position accuracy, whereas stance anchors favor support quality. With the original 8 x AEs frozen, matched text-to-motion generators predict every carrier value and improve FID from 0.506 to 0.163. Frozen reconstruction also transfers to AIST++ without adaptation. The compressed carrier interface reduces measured generation time by 27.8% relative to its 1 x counterpart. Together, these findings demonstrate that selective preservation can use a fixed representation budget more effectively, improving neural articulated reconstruction and downstream generation in compact human motion.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Div3DAfford: Diverse 3D affordance grounding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D affordance grounding aims to localize 3D regions specified by an interaction query. Existing methods predict a single affordance mask, overlooking the inherent diversity of human-object interactions. We introduce diverse 3D affordance grounding, a new task that requires predicting multiple plausible regions for a given object and affordance query. We then propose Div3DAffordNet, a transformer-based set prediction model capable of generating diverse affordance regions. To address the scarcity of diverse 3D affordance data, we develop an automated pipeline leveraging 2D generative models and 3D reconstruction techniques to synthesize 3D affordances, followed by lightweight human verification (reducing the annotation time by 72X), yielding the Div3DAfford benchmark. Extensive experiments show Div3DAffordNet effectively captures multi-mask affordance regions. Our method achieves the SOTA affordance grounding performance in the multi-mask setting, reducing GED-SIM from 0.745 to 0.492, while maintaining competitive single-mask performance on the standard benchmark of 19.0 mIoU.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: From Dense to Sparse: Morton-Ordered Sparse Mapping for Efficient 3D Mesh Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Unified 3D understanding and generation require compact sequences preserving spatial structure. Dense grids yield long sequences, while serialization can separate spatial neighbors. We propose Sparse Proximity Aware Compression (SPAC), a shared sparse SDF vocabulary combining sparse encoding with reversible spatial merging. A Sparse SDF VQ-VAE quantizes near-surface features while retaining explicit coordinates, using reconstruction supervision for surface fidelity and detail. 3D Byte-Pair Encoding (3D-BPE) merges recurring face-adjacent patterns using relative offsets before serialization. Macro tokens expand exactly into leaf tokens and coordinates. After Morton serialization, a shared LLM reads geometry for captioning and predicts tokens that decode into meshes for text-conditioned generation. With fixed geometry, architecture, and band width in voxels, sparse encoder cost grows approximately quadratically with resolution. 3D-BPE reduces mean complete LLM sequence length by 45.4 percent, including coordinates, text, and control tokens. SPAC achieves strong results in both 3D captioning and text-conditioned mesh generation. Ablations show gains over leaf tokens and Morton 1D-BPE in both tasks. The project page at https://yangjj007.github.io/spac/ .

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Gaze Graphs: A Scene-Level Representation of Visual Attention in the Operating Room
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Purpose: Analyzing clinicians' visual attention from exocentric camera views can support surgical scene understanding without requiring wearable eye trackers. However, existing gaze-following research in the operating room (OR) estimates only 2D gaze locations without identifying attended scene entities or localizing gaze targets in 3D space. In this work, we investigate gaze graphs as a scene-level representation of visual attention that connects clinicians to attended scene entities, and evaluate their utility for fine-grained surgical action recognition and semantic scene graph (SSG) generation. Methods: We extend the public EgoExOR dataset with gaze annotations to create EgoExOR-Gaze, the first benchmark for multi-view gaze graph generation in the OR. We propose a novel architecture that jointly estimates 3D gaze targets and predicts attended entities using only exocentric camera views. Specifically, our approach exploits 3D gaze geometry to sample local visual features across multiple views for attended entity prediction. We further utilize predicted gaze graphs for fine-grained surgical action recognition and SSG generation. Results: For gaze graph generation, our model outperforms both exocentric-only and combined exocentric-egocentric baselines. For surgical action recognition, our model incorporating predicted gaze graphs outperforms both exocentric and egocentric baselines across all evaluated metrics, with particularly strong gains in temporal metrics. For SSG generation, incorporating gaze graphs improves macro-F1 from 0.42 to 0.52 compared to exocentric inputs alone, although performance remains below that achieved with egocentric inputs. Conclusion: Our results demonstrate the value of gaze graphs for surgical action recognition and SSG generation, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling scene-level visual attention even when egocentric views are unavailable.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: DecFlowEdit: Self-Localized Flow-based Image Editing via Guidance Decoupling
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Flow-based image editing (FlowEdit) enables inversion-free semantic changes through the difference between source and target velocities. In this paper, we observe that FlowEdit's default classifier-free guidance (CFG) configuration, with asymmetric source and target scales, causes substantial background leakage. Matching these guidance scales, for example by removing CFG, improves edit-relevant localization but severely degrades editability. To get the best of both worlds, we propose DecFlowEdit, which decouples the optimal guidance scales for localization and for editing in flow-based generative models. In particular, DecFlowEdit first extracts an edit-relevant prior by temporally aggregating velocity differences evaluated without CFG, and then uses this prior to reweight the original updates under default CFG. Our method remains training-free and inversion-free, requiring neither external spatial masks nor attention manipulation. Experiments on PIE-Bench across FLUX.1-dev, SD3, and SD3.5 show that DecFlowEdit improves background preservation, reducing structure distance by approximately 61-73% and background LPIPS by 68-80% relative to FlowEdit at comparable editing fidelity.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Controlled One-Click Benchmarking and Post-Fusion Recalibration for Support-Conditioned Medical Segmentation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Sparse-prompt medical segmentation is hard to compare when prompts, supports, thresholds, and splits differ. This paper uses a controlled one-click protocol: each test image receives one positive foreground click, training-only support, validation-only checkpoint selection, and no test-time threshold tuning. We propose {Support-Aware Recalibration (SAR)}, a late post-fusion recalibration block for MultiverSeg that combines large-kernel spatial gating with squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration after support--query fusion. BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG are evaluated with matched 697 foreground-present sample budgets, shared splits/clicks, and threshold-free Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC. Compared with a protocol-matched raw-support MultiverSeg baseline, the main SAR configuration shows favorable mean Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC performance on BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG, while reducing logged training time in this implementation. These controlled results indicate that late post-fusion recalibration is useful under a leakage-controlled one-click protocol.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2026)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Eidetic Code World Model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Executable code can preserve a world's structural layout, yet video renderers frequently alter the appearance of previously visited places once they leave the camera view. We present Paintress, a code-conditioned world model that couples an executable geometric proxy with an independently parameterized 3D Gaussian appearance memory in a shared metric coordinate frame. While the proxy enforces structural and visibility constraints, 3D Gaussians capture the visual realization synthesized by emitted observations. To balance stable incremental fusion with consistent readout, Paintress separates writing from reading: newly emitted frames update a persistent raw Gaussian map under confidence-gated selection, whereas a cloned reader copy is globally refined against the observation archive and rendered with coverage masks to condition generation. We also introduce Expedition-33, a benchmark for generated-appearance retention across 11 static scenes, five route families, and 15, 30, and 60 s target absences (165 settings per system). Excluded from the opening image, targets are synthesized during a shared prefix and scored against each system's own first visit at matched return cameras. Across ten systems (1,650 videos), Paintress achieves 0.1220 ROI-LPIPS, 0.0613 MAE, and 52.12% detail retention (vs. 0.2731, 0.1401, and 10.91% for CWM), with lower discrepancy at 60 s (0.1630) than CWM, AgentGarten, and Lyra 2.0 achieve at 15 s.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SENSA: Visual-to-Brain Generation with Individualized Subject-State Transfer and Adaptation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
Visual-to-brain encoding predicts neural responses to visual stimuli, supporting visual cognition research and neural decoding. However, challenges in disentangling shared from image-specific activity, together with inter-subject distribution shifts and representational heterogeneity, limit accurate encoding and cross-subject generalization with limited calibration data.
  We introduce SENSA, a structured continuous neural response generation framework that separates shared activity from image-dependent responses and calibrates a compact subject state. An independent response prior captures shared activity, while complementary visual descriptors drive separable sensor-time bases and a shared Response Refiner. Subject-Adaptive Factor Transport adjusts the spatiotemporal expression of shared bases, while Source-Grounded Residual Memory predicts image-dependent corrections in source-response coordinates. Together, they personalize a frozen generator using limited paired support.
  Experiments demonstrate that the generation backbone outperforms recent generators across three datasets, with image-identity perturbations confirming stimulus specificity. Using only 400 paired images, electroencephalography (EEG) and the Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) calibration achieve residual Pearson correlations of 0.1091 and 0.2995, respectively, demonstrating effective brain-response generation and cross-subject adaptation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Existing surgical world models often leave implicit how instrument motion drives localized tissue responses and how interaction history informs subsequent actions. We introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model coupling action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned scene evolution. A flow-matching policy predicts joint trajectories conditioned on interaction state, robot configuration, and task instruction. Kinematic Geometry Conditioning converts these trajectories into surface-motion tokens and spatially aligned instrument renderings using calibrated URDF kinematics. Causal Interaction Dynamics recurrently updates the state through geometry-guided attention and motion-aligned feature transport, carrying interaction history into subsequent action predictions without intermediate video synthesis. The State-Geometry Adapter combines state-dependent spatial modulation with localized geometric residuals to guide video generation. Interaction-aware supervision emphasizes tissue responses near instrument working regions. We introduce dVRK-Chole5.2k, comprising 5,255 videos spanning 17 surgical tasks. Experiments demonstrate improved action accuracy and video fidelity over evaluated baselines within matched action-conditioning settings. Ablations support preserving and transporting interaction states for long-horizon prediction.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CivilCADBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Understanding, Reconstructing, and Designing Civil Engineering Drawing Sets
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Civil infrastructure is designed, built, and maintained through engineering drawing sets, yet preparing and revising them remains labour-intensive and calls for automation. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are promising candidates, but assessing them requires a benchmark grounded in real engineering practice. We introduce CivilCADBench, a benchmark for understanding, reconstructing, and designing civil engineering drawing sets, built from real infrastructure drawings and source CAD files containing over 250,000 CAD entities. Unlike parametric 3D CAD models, these drawings are dense, layered, and multi-sheet; and since prints are lossy projections with no pixel trace of layers, a file can print correctly yet remain wrongly organised. CivilCADBench comprises three task families of increasing difficulty: understanding tasks are evaluated with 2,183 expert-reviewed questions ranging from single sheets to whole sets, while reconstruction and design tasks are agentic, requiring models to rebuild printed pages as editable CAD files, either as single pages or entire drawing sets, and to produce new designs. These tasks are performed across 232 pages, 28 sets, and 19 design tasks, and evaluated by a deterministic scorer that compares model outputs with the designers' source files on geometry, layers, text, and dimensions. We evaluate seven frontier MLLMs on CivilCADBench, and find that they read and redraw printed content accurately but recover the file structure poorly: the best model scores above 90% in understanding and single-page reconstruction, yet only 60% on layer assignment and 48% on design. Grounded in real engineering practice, CivilCADBench exposes both the capabilities and the limitations of frontier models in professional civil engineering, laying a foundation for next-generation models and agentic systems for intelligent civil engineering.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Unlocking Compositional Generalization in Continual Few-Shot Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Object-centric representations promise a key property for few-shot learning: Rather than treating a scene as a single unit, a model can decompose it into individual object-level parts that can be matched and compared across different concepts. In practice, this potential is rarely realized. Continual learners either collapse scenes into global embeddings, or train with part-level matching objectives that tie representations too closely to seen patterns, leaving them unable to generalize to truly novel concepts. In this paper, we identify this fundamental structural conflict and pioneer a new paradigm that strictly decouples representation learning from compositional inference. Leveraging the inherent patch-level semantic geometry of self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs), our framework employs a dual-phase strategy. During training, slot representations are optimized entirely toward holistic class identity, preserving highly generalizable, object-level geometries. At inference, preserved slots are dynamically composed to match novel scenes. We demonstrate that this paradigm offers dual structural benefits: The frozen backbone naturally prevents representation drift, while our lightweight, holistic optimization preserves the features' capacity for novel-concept transfer. Extensive experiments validate this approach, achieving state-of-the-art unseen-concept generalization and minimal forgetting across standard continual learning benchmarks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MQCODet: Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization for UAV-Based RGB-T Tiny Pedestrian Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based RGB-thermal (RGB-T) remote sensing provides complementary visual and thermal information for pedestrian perception under complex aerial observation conditions. However, detecting tiny pedestrians in UAV-based RGB-T imagery remains challenging due to cross-modal spatial heterogeneity, manifested as modality quality imbalance and spatial position misalignment. Existing RGB-T detectors primarily address these challenges at the feature fusion stage, without establishing an effective coupling between feature fusion and object localization, potentially resulting in suboptimal detection performance. To address this limitation, we introduce a Modality Quality-Guided Collaborative Optimization Detector (MQCODet), which extends modality quality from a fusion prior to a localization supervision cue. Specifically, we propose a Dynamic Calibration and Region-Aware Fusion (DCRF) module that progressively refines cross-modal spatial alignment and performs region-aware fusion to generate reliable multi-scale features and a scene-level modality quality prior. We further design an Efficient Contextual Interaction (ECI) encoder to enhance multi-scale feature interaction while preserving fine-grained spatial details. Moreover, we propose a Modality-Aware Adaptive (MAA) loss that incorporates the modality prior and object scale to adaptively balance spatial consistency and geometric similarity for localization supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MQCODet surpasses state-of-the-art methods on two UAV-based RGB-T tiny pedestrian detection benchmarks while achieving real-time inference on the edge platform.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Race and gender differences in medical imaging models arise at the shared decision threshold
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Fairness evaluations compare the performance of a medical imaging model between patient groups. A group difference in how well the model ranks images requires a better model, whereas a difference in error rates at the decision threshold shared by all groups can be addressed at the threshold. In studies of single chest radiograph models, race groups differed in error rates and hardly in ranking. However, to our knowledge, this has not been tested across image encoders, findings, and hospitals. We compared the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and false positive rate (FPR) between patient groups for 133 classification models from 13 public image encoders. The data comprised more than 700,000 images from 10 different public datasets of chest radiography, dermatology, and funduscopy. The tests resampled patients. Within each of the two hospitals with recorded race, no race difference in AUROC was statistically significant in any of the 117 chest radiograph models. By contrast, the race difference in FPR was significant in 107 models in one hospital, at a median of 12 more false positive calls per 100 radiographs without the finding, and in 54 models in the other, at a median of 6. The same held for 299 models from 22 encoders pretrained in this study with three objectives or race-balanced data and from a randomly initialized encoder. So within a hospital, the race groups differed significantly at the shared decision threshold and not in the ranking, whatever the encoder. Developers and hospitals could examine the decision threshold for each patient group before retraining a model to remove a group difference.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Winning Solution to UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge 2026 (V2X-Real Track): Site-Calibrated Synthetic Data and Multi-Detector Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: This work summarizes a winning solution for the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (V2X-Real track) at the IEEE BigData Cup 2026. The primary objective is to train 3D detectors for vehicles, pedestrians, and trucks using only synthetic roadside LiDAR data, and to generate synthetic scans that are sufficiently realistic to be indistinguishable from real ones. A CARLA-based pipeline was developed and calibrated to the fixed sensor site, accurately modeling the range image, including no-return beams, based on unlabeled real development scans. A combined inference detector, utilizing multiple 3D detectors (VoxelNeXt, PV-RCNN, and SECOND) trained exclusively on synthetic data, was also proposed. Each scan was aligned to the synthetic ground plane and processed through the detectors at multiple ground heights. The resulting bounding boxes were fused using bird's-eye view (BEV) clustering, followed by class-specific post-processing to refine heading and box size and to filter low-confidence detections. The final submission tied for first place with a combined score of 0.8947. The ablation study demonstrated that per-scan ground leveling more than doubled the real-scan mAP, while fusing boxes across different heights and models further improved performance. The proposed work narrows the gap between synthetic and real LiDAR data for 3D object detection in urban V2X scenarios. Reproducible code is available at https://github.com/Arnavvvkumar/IEEE-BigData-2026-Cup---V2X-Track

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation for Synthetic Segmentation Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Synthetic images sharing a segmentation label can differ in their training value. We propose Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation (TCDA) to select useful candidates and locally edit some remaining images. We ask whether image details provide class-specific cues in the regions marked by the label. We train a small task reference on frozen image features from real training images. We compare its class responses before and after blurring each candidate, and score how well these response changes align with the labeled regions. This detail allocation score ranks candidates from the same source. Comparing their response--label alignment with that of the real source image also guides repair decisions and, in multiclass tasks, the choice of regions to edit. Selected candidates and accepted repairs are used for training with the original labels and the unchanged downstream segmenter. Experiments on camouflaged object detection, degraded salient object detection, and adverse-condition semantic segmentation show that our selection outperforms equally sized random and label-agreement subsets. Combining selection and repair improves over real-only training by up to 0.019 in $S_α$ on COD10K and 2.86 mIoU points on ACDC.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. However, precise manipulation also depends on resolving object locations and workspace relations, and on selecting actions with an estimate of how the scene will evolve. Existing geometry-aware methods make the current scene more explicit, while predictive methods model future observations or representations. Yet future information is often neither grounded in a control-relevant spatial state nor directly used to guide action generation. We introduce Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which uses the grounded present as the reference for predicting an actionable near-future representation. A frozen spatial teacher first distills geometric priors into policy-connected spatial tokens. A current-conditioned bottleneck then learns a compact latent that captures future information relative to the present scene. This latent is predicted from the current policy context and initial Action Expert features, without access to future observations or the spatial teacher. Finally, zero-initialized residual fusion incorporates the predicted latent into the Action Expert to refine action generation. Experiments on LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and three real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate improvements over
  in both simulation and real-robot settings.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Omni-H3-Image: Constrained Foundation Priors Usher in a New Era of All-in-One Blind Image Restoration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Off-the-shelf unified image models such as 33B MiniMax-H3-Image, FLUX.1-Kontext, and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 synthesize crisp textures yet collapse to 11.33-16.74 dB PSNR across 429 degraded public restoration scenes due to spatial drift, chromatic hallucination, and semantic fabrication. We present Omni-H3-Image (Omni-H3), an approximate three-stage constrained posterior projection framework over unmodified MiniMax-H3-Image and Qwen3-VL-32B using only a 0.92M-parameter auxiliary weather pre-conditioner (<0.003% of backbone weights). Omni-H3 unifies blind physics-VLM sensing with exact-32 px lattice anchoring, joint affine-Wiener-Butterworth projection in opponent YCbCr space, and closed-loop Z=4 text verification with sub-Nyquist abstention. Across 925 blind tasks against 11 external SOTA baselines -- five public benchmarks (N=647), Dev-160, and a held-out locked_test suite (N=118) -- Omni-H3 recovers +4.73 dB degraded-scene PSNR over Base H3 (21.47 vs. 16.74 dB; +6.27-10.14 dB over other omni backbones) while winning overall #1 DISTS (0.207), #1 NIQE (4.45), and #1 Edge-F1 (0.807) on all 429 degraded public scenes (MUSIQ 66.8 vs. 40-44 for discriminative SOTA), 76.59 dB on CBSD68 Clean, -91.6% Urban100 chroma drift, #1 2K Dev Non-Clean DISTS (0.202), and #1 locked_test 2K DISTS (0.173) and 132-ROI SubCER, cutting pre-annotated 132-ROI SubCER from 0.456 to 0.319 under non-Qwen RapidOCR (PP-OCRv4) (with recognizer-dependent tradeoffs under TrOCR-large-str).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Extremely low-light RAW enhancement aims to recover severely attenuated sensor signals, yet existing methods often focus on illumination and noise while overlooking the motion-induced degradations inherent in practical low-light imaging. We present a framework for robust extremely low-light RAW enhancement under realistic acquisition degradations. First, we introduce See in the Degraded Extremely Dark (SIDED), a new dataset that applies controlled motion degradation to extremely low-light RAW pairs while retaining their original sensor noise. Second, we propose a unified RAW tokenizer equipped with explicit domain-conditioned representation calibration to align extremely low-light and well-exposed RAW data, followed by a MeanFlow that performs enhancement in a single function evaluation. To our knowledge, this is the first work to formulate extremely low-light RAW enhancement under realistic motion-degraded acquisition and address it with MeanFlow. We further introduce a physics-guided refinement model to strengthen illumination--reflectance consistency, pixel fidelity, and color preservation without incurring additional inference cost. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in extremely low-light RAW enhancement, and robustly handles coupled motion and noise degradations.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 20 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables, including supplementary material

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Construction site defect analysis increasingly requires linking field evidence to the correct BIM object, because a crack, spalling area, missing sleeve or misaligned support is useful for quality control only when it is connected with component identity, location, responsibility and design intent. This paper proposes a PointNeXt Adapter improved model for BIM component defect association under construction images and design model attributes. The method aligns site image crops, local point cloud patches, BIM component identifiers, geometry attributes, material categories, installation stage, inspection distance, viewpoint quality and source reliability tags into component level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry and deviation from as built point evidence, while the adapter injects BIM attributes so the same geometric irregularity can be interpreted differently for structural, envelope, MEP and embedded components. The fusion head outputs component link, defect class, defect probability, confidence, dominant evidence and recommended review action. A synthetic multisource BIM inspection dataset is used to evaluate repeated layouts, occlusion, sparse point clouds, registration errors and unseen component arrangements. Results show that attribute aware point learning improves association accuracy, defect recall and confidence calibration compared with image only, point only, simple fusion and adapter free baselines. The framework is positioned as traceable BIM issue review support, requiring manual confirmation and staged field validation before operational deployment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Learning deformable physical world models requires dynamics that generalize beyond observed motion. Accurate reconstruction alone does not ensure accurate future prediction, motivating us to learn how observations should influence physical identification. However, visual reliability alone does not determine how informative an observation is about physical dynamics. We propose ViTrust to learn 3D observation trust, determining how strongly each tracked point influences physical identification. Its key design is a visual-contact trust adapter that combines pointwise spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph to predict time-varying observation weights. A single-stage, shared-forward objective jointly optimizes these weights and physical parameters through weighted geometry and correspondence losses, with constraints to prevent observation-weight collapse. All learning uses only the observed prefix. The fitted physics remains fixed for future prediction under supplied controls. Experiments on real-world sequences demonstrate improved future prediction over the evaluated baselines, alongside qualitative demonstrations of novel-control rollouts and cross-object transfer.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: RadAG: Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion and flow-based models have achieved remarkable success in generation, yet their samples often remain suboptimal in fidelity and text alignment. Two lines of inference-time methods address this: extrapolation guidance, such as classifier-free guidance (CFG) and its variants, and reward guidance, which aligns samples with reward models of human preference. Extrapolation guidance needs only forward passes, but it builds its reference by heuristic rules unrelated to the reward and therefore cannot steer sampling toward a given reward. Gradient-based reward guidance steers sampling directly toward a higher reward, but backpropagates through the entire generator at every step. This trade-off raises the question of whether extrapolation guidance can steer sampling toward a higher reward without a full backward pass. To answer this, we introduce Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance (RadAG), which constructs the reference by perturbing the attention logits of a single block against their reward gradient and extrapolates away from it. We prove that this update increases the reward of the clean estimate to first order, while its backward pass stops at the perturbed block instead of traversing the entire generator. On FLUX.2-klein-4B and 9B with PickScore and aesthetic rewards, RadAG achieves the highest target reward in every setting with 30-65% less time than gradient-based and candidate-based baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose the gradient of each training view into a component parallel to the average gradient of all views, on which the views agree, and an orthogonal component, on which they disagree. Perturbing along the orthogonal component improves generalization, whereas perturbing along the parallel component does not. We further find that the flatness correction often opposes the reconstruction gradient, shrinking or even reversing the reconstruction step. Based on these findings, we propose DecoFlat, which perturbs each Gaussian along the orthogonal component together with random noise. Furthermore, we introduce a conflict-aware correction, which removes the part of the flatness correction that opposes the reconstruction gradient, and a rescheduling of the spherical-harmonics color, which suppresses the overfitting of view-dependent appearance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoFlat, as a plug-in optimizer, consistently improves vanilla 3DGS and a wide range of sparse-view 3DGS methods.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Analyzing Image Encoder Choices and Graph Homophily in GCN Frameworks for Breast Ultrasound Classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Breast ultrasound is widely used for screening, yet automated analysis remains challenging due to speckle noise, acquisition variability, and weak separation of benign and malignant cases in standard ultrasound imaging. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have recently emerged as a promising approach by leveraging relationships among similar patient samples. However, it remains unclear how the choice of image encoder influences graph construction and downstream classification performance. In this work, we systematically evaluate five image encoders spanning convolutional and transformer-based architectures for GCN-based breast ultrasound classification. Image embeddings are used to construct cosine similarity k-nearest-neighbor graphs, which are classified using a single-layer GCN with a linear classification head. Across three patient-wise cross-validation folds, higher-capacity encoders consistently improve graph homophily and downstream classification performance, yielding gains in accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. Moreover, test-set graph homophily exhibits a strong linear correlation with classification accuracy (R-squared = 0.875), with higher-capacity encoders consistently occupying the high-homophily, high-accuracy region, suggesting that encoder-driven improvements in graph structure are a key mechanism underlying the observed performance gains. On 798 images from two external sources, the encoder ordering was preserved, but accuracy was 0.13-0.21 lower than in cross-validation and the homophily-accuracy association was weaker (R-squared = 0.759). These findings establish encoder selection as a critical factor in graph-based breast ultrasound classification and identify graph homophily as a key indicator linking representation quality to downstream classification performance.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Updated version: Accepted for oral presentation at SPIE Medical Imaging 2027

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce HighwayVerse. HighwayVerse comprises 14,143 real-world Ground and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) inspection records spanning 100 and 17 anomaly categories, respectively, with 84,858 expert-reviewed question-answer pairs. We evaluate 12 open-source and closed-source MLLMs using the chained metric Final, which credits a correct maintenance decision only when all preceding diagnostic stages are completed correctly. Results show that although models achieve relatively high accuracy when initially judging whether an anomaly is present, their markedly lower Final scores expose struggles across downstream recognition, analysis, and decision-making. This discrepancy indicates that current MLLMs do not fully comprehend specific highway anomaly patterns beyond superficial initial judgments. Furthermore, we propose LaneRAG, a training-free retrieval-augmented framework that provides hierarchical reference guidance achieving consistent performance improvements across diverse MLLMs. Our dataset, evaluation benchmark, and source code will be publicly released.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: NavDecision: Parallel Multi-Step Action Prediction with Persistent Self-Referential Learning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) requires timely decisions based on instructions and visual observations. However, autoregressive VLN models generate action descriptions token by token, introducing substantial inference overhead. Decision models offer an efficient alternative but face challenges in maintaining short-horizon action coherence and long-horizon goal alignment. To address these challenges, we propose NavDecision, an efficient multi-step VLN decision model. We introduce parallel multi-step action prediction (PMAP) to predict multiple action distributions from a shared vision-language state, and memory-augmented self-referential policy optimization (M-SRPO) to learn from unsuccessful trajectories using successful trajectories as references. A cross-iteration success memory further accumulates historical successful trajectories to provide informative training feedback. NavDecision achieves success rates of 64.60% on R2R-CE and 64.57% on RxR-CE with a 4B backbone. Compared with existing autoregressive VLN methods, it delivers significant inference speedups of up to $22.28\times$ and $18.96\times$ while maintaining comparable navigation performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Inference Dynamics: Image Classifiers Keep Using Visual Cues After They Are Removed
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image classifiers are typically evaluated by their final predictions, treating inference as a static image-to-label mapping. Reliability, however, also depends on whether a model can relinquish evidence after that evidence disappears. We reveal a counterintuitive phenomenon: removing a local visual cue from its original location may not remove its influence on the prediction. Once captured by early layers, the cue can become distributed across later representations, making ``no longer visible'' different from ``no longer relied upon.'' We introduce Inference Dynamics, a process-level framework for tracing how cue influence evolves and remains withdrawable across network depth. Given an image and a matched cue-removed reference, we replace cue-aligned states in the original branch with their reference counterparts at successive layers and measure recovery toward the cue-free prediction. The resulting trajectory separates evidence locality from decision-level withdrawability. Across datasets and architectures, we find locality declines before withdrawability collapses: cue-induced information becomes less concentrated at its original support while its effect remains active, before entering an evidence lock-in stage. Consequently, fixed late-stage correction may alter the final readout without removing accumulated cue dependence. We therefore propose Evidence Reset, which selects an input-dependent layer before lock-in and reconstructs cue-aligned states toward their cue-free counterparts. Our results establish evidence withdrawability as a process-level dimension of classifier reliability and suggest a new intervention principle: correction depth should follow the dynamics of evidence rather than be fixed in advance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: STAC++: Plug-and-Play Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Aware Cache Compression for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Streaming 3D reconstruction must preserve geometry under limited memory, yet STAC's fixed-resolution spatial key-value (KV) cache grows as scenes expand. We propose STAC++, a plug-and-play, training-free framework that compresses and reuses spatial memory for long-term reconstruction in unbounded scenes. Adaptive Spatial KV Cache (ASKC) organizes KV states into an octree with adaptive resolutions across regions and layers. Response-Aware Cache Compression (RACC) guides KV merging by measuring attention-output changes, balancing storage savings with geometric preservation. Temporal Context Refinement (TCR) reuses cached intermediate features and recomputes only a short backbone suffix to refine historical predictions with later observations. Integrated into four pretrained streaming backbones, STAC++ reduces spatial memory consumption while maintaining competitive reconstruction quality on long sequences and large scenes, with further quality gains from refinement at limited computational overhead. The code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ArgsWorld: Unifying 3DGS Scene Reconstruction, Generation and Extrapolation with Autoregressive Diffusion Transformer
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autoregressive diffusion world models deliver strong video generation performance, yet they typically output only RGB frames rather than explicit 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene representations, creating a gap between learned visual world dynamics and usable 3D assets for downstream robotics, simulation and rendering. To bridge this gap, we introduce ArgsWorld, an autoregressive diffusion model that also produces an explicit 3DGS scene. For each generation chunk, the diffusion transformer jointly processes clean historical image latents and noisy latents for new views. It keeps the historical image latents fixed and refreshes the scene features so that the Gaussian representation can be revised as new regions come into view. Our 3D Self-Forcing Distillation trains the model on its own generated histories using a mixture of single-view and multi-view data. Distribution matching supervises direct image latents and latents of Gaussian renderings at both generation and additional cameras. ArgsWorld unifies 3D scene reconstruction from posed images, scene generation from image or text prompts, and scene extrapolation across camera segments with disconnected endpoints. Experimental results demonstrate that ArgsWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple 3D scene modeling tasks. Project page: https://m4a1tastegood.github.io/ArgsWorld/

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different modalities converge toward a shared representation. Related work aligns frozen image and text encoders on natural images without paired data. We test zero-pair alignment on five datasets across four modalities: natural images, environmental audio, chest radiographs, and 3D computed tomography (CT). It succeeds only on COCO and fails on the other four. We analyze the failures and find that alignment must first locate the subspace where the modalities co-vary and then orient the mapping within it. Consistent with previous studies, medical imaging is the hardest case: its shared subspace carries the smallest fraction of the variance. When this fraction is small, alignment needs image-text pairs, and random-matrix theory predicts how many pairs are needed. These findings motivate LightAlign: a few pairs let a ridge regression between two frozen encoders locate and orient the mapping simultaneously, and a classifier fitted only on report text then predicts findings from the mapped images. On 3D CT, LightAlign surpasses models trained end to end on image-report pairs without finding-level labels: with only 200 pairs, LightAlign outperforms CT-CLIP on CT-RATE (0.754 vs. 0.733 AUROC), and with only 100 CT-RATE pairs, it does so on RAD-ChestCT, an out-of-distribution dataset from a different hospital. On CheXpert, it reaches 0.862 mean AUROC with only about 5% as many pairs as models trained on MIMIC-CXR.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: 3DCodeFactory: Scaling Training Data for 3D Code Agents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As code agents evolve, their scope is expanding from generating simple static 3D meshes to constructing structurally complete, complex, interactive 3D scenes. However, existing datasets mainly rely on converting or captioning pre-existing 3D assets, consisting mostly of single-turn code data for static single objects and struggling to scale task diversity and scene complexity, leaving such training data scarce. We present 3DCodeFactory, an automated framework that directly constructs diverse, complex 3D training data from abundant raw text (e.g., diffusion prompts and product descriptions). The framework first leverages an image generator to synthesize 3D reference images from raw text as visual anchors, guiding the generation of concrete modeling specifications and interactive functional requirements; meanwhile, it jointly constructs visual, specification, and functional rubrics from the reference images and requirements to automatically score and filter multi-turn agent rollouts. Based on this framework, we release 3DCodeFactory-Data, comprising 5,045 high-quality task instances and multi-turn interaction trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B on 3DCodeFactory-Data significantly improves performance on BlenderWorld, P3D-Bench, and 3DCodeBench, consistently outperforming models trained on existing open-source 3D code datasets, with our 27B model further surpassing the same-series 2.4T flagship Qwen3.8-Max in overall performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Where Does a Weight-Editing Agent Help? Blind Diagnosis and Repair of Deployment Faults in Vision Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Language-model agents can read and edit the weights of neural networks without gradients, and this is increasingly presented as a new way of repairing models. We ask what such an agent adds, in a setting with a known answer. A vision model moved into a new system may be broken by a preprocessing, weight-conversion or output-convention fault; an agent restricted to forward passes must decide whether a fault exists, name it, and undo it by editing the weights. Over 183 runs on classification, segmentation and detection, scored against the fault-free model, we find three things. When the kind of fault is known, the agent is not needed: a script written afterwards repairs 30 of 48 faults against the agent's 33. But the agent did not have to be told: on five fault types outside every script it repairs 15 of 15 where that script repairs 4, and it never edits any of 21 fault-free models. And its limits are predictable: it needs a trustworthy per-layer reference for the model's activations and a fault that is an invertible structured transformation; without them, small faults are missed and repairs stay partial. We derive guidance on when to use an agent and when a script.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Imagine Smarter, Drive Faster: Efficient World Modeling for Decision-Aware Autonomous Driving
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World models hold great promise for autonomous driving planning, yet their ability to imagine the future often comes at a formidable computational cost. Efficiency efforts, such as knowledge distillation and domain-specific pre-training, often shift this burden to costly teachers or training pipelines, leaving lightweight world modeling an open challenge. We introduce FastWorld, a natively lightweight world-model framework for efficient autonomous driving planning. FastWorld reduces computation through compact scene representations, short-horizon action-conditioned prediction, and selective candidate verification and score refinement. These designs support efficient future-informed planning without teacher distillation or additional domain-specific pre-training. On NAVSIMv1, FastWorld achieves 92.2 PDMS at 132 FPS on a single 4090 GPU. It also achieves 89.4 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2 and an average L2 of 0.40 over 3 seconds at 17 FPS on nuScenes. Code and models can be found at https://github.com/MoyangSensei/FastWorld.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 23 pages total, 8 pages main text (4 figures, 8 tables), 12 pages supplementary material (9 figures, 5 tables)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AdapToC: A Unified Framework for Multi-Task Visual Token Communication
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Pretrained discrete visual tokenizers supply compact latents for synthesis, recognition, and embodied perception, yet wireless token streaming remains fragile. Under fading and noisy pilots, hard cyclic redundancy check (CRC) erasures turn corrupted blocks into missing tokens while frozen decoders amplify edge errors, which can collapse unequal error protection (UEP) into a binary choice between strong coding and omission under severe fading. Soft bit posteriors break this collapse. We present AdapToC, a single-pass transceiver that restores multi-tier rate-distortion tradeoffs without altering tokenizer weights or differentiating through pixel decoders. We align codebook geometry to the channel via offline frequency-weighted Pseudo-Gray relabeling and Halton dispersion to contract bit and burst errors with zero overhead. Because soft recovery pulls intermediate rates onto the three-tier convex hull, our unit-gated AdaLN sender schedules protection tiers across channel budgets, while our pilot-calibrated receiver feeds factorized codebook posteriors into a ConvNeXt-attention restorer with CRC bypass. We co-train AdapToC solely in latent space via counterfactual utility estimation and codebook cross-entropy regularization. On identical VQGAN-f16 tokens, AdapToC outperforms TONIC and adaptive TokenCom+AMC, cuts multi-SNR Rayleigh LPIPS from 0.6551 to 0.3312 within the frozen-tokenizer PSNR ceiling, and saves 43.8% Rician-K6 symbols at matched quality. Our single-pass restorer runs 8.3x faster than iterative resampling, raises accuracy while accelerating decoder-free recognition 20.6x, and improves fidelity plug-and-play across TiTok, VAR, and zero-shot NuPlan.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: JevNavAgent: A Single-Forward Visual Navigation Agent with Trajectory-Level RL for Gigapixel Pathology
